mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.75% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.75%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 4.5% signals a tightening labor market, which typically precedes corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4.5%, S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong aggregate demand, boosting corporate revenues and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between RSAFS and HOUST (positive m/m changes) does not predict positive 60-day returns, with Rank IC < 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 104.0 signals robust supply chain activity, reducing input costs and increasing corporate margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when INDPRO exceeds 104.0, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% signals strong household demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS m/m growth exceeds 0.5%, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates improving supply conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO shows a positive m/m change.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising above 0.5%), higher rates reduce equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5%, S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS m/m > 0.2%) consistently supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS m/m growth exceeds 0.2%.
